title: Divided Monarchy — Regnal Evaluations (Deuteronomistic verdicts)
purpose: Drives the regnal-evaluation timeline (Guide B). Let the repeating 'did right / did evil' formula be the visual.
source: KJV via vault ScriptureDatabase; every verdict + reign-length verified verbatim from 1–2 Kings
chronology_note: reign_years_text are the figures the text states (co-regencies/synchronisms make these overlap). Absolute BCE dates are intentionally null — set them from a chosen chronology (recommended: Edwin Thiele, 'The Mysterious Numbers of the Hebrew Kings'). Do NOT invent dates.

verdict_legend.right: 'did right in the eyes/sight of the LORD'
verdict_legend.evil: 'did evil in the sight of the LORD'

israel.note: every northern king is judged evil — the visual point

judah.name: Rehoboam
judah.evaluation_quote: And Judah did evil in the sight of the LORD…
judah.summary: Solomon's son, whose harsh answer at Shechem split the kingdom (1 Kings 12). In his fifth year Egypt's Pharaoh Shishak sacked Jerusalem and carried off the temple's gold (1 Kings 14:25–26).

judah.name: Abijam
judah.evaluation_quote: he walked in all the sins of his father… his heart was not perfect with the LORD
judah.summary: Warred with Jeroboam of the North; the record faults him — 'his heart was not perfect with the LORD' — yet for David's sake Judah's lamp was kept burning (1 Kings 15:3–4).

judah.name: Asa
judah.evaluation_quote: Asa did that which was right in the eyes of the LORD, as did David his father
judah.summary: Judah's first reforming king — he swept out idols and even removed the queen mother Maacah for her Asherah image (1 Kings 15:11–13). A long, largely faithful reign.

judah.name: Jehoshaphat
judah.evaluation_quote: doing that which was right… nevertheless the high places were not taken away
judah.summary: A righteous, prosperous king who set judges across the land — but his marriage-alliance with Ahab's house pulled Judah into the North's wars (1 Kings 22). The high places remained.

judah.name: Jehoram
judah.evaluation_quote: he walked in the way of the kings of Israel… and he did evil
judah.summary: Married Athaliah of Ahab's house and walked in the way of the kings of Israel (2 Kings 8:18). Edom threw off Judah's rule in his reign.

judah.name: Ahaziah
judah.evaluation_quote: walked in the way of the house of Ahab, and did evil
judah.summary: Reigned a single year, tied through his mother Athaliah to Ahab's house — and was caught up and killed in Jehu's northern purge (2 Kings 9:27).

judah.name: Athaliah
judah.evaluation_quote: And Athaliah did reign over the land
judah.summary: Ahab's daughter, and the one break in David's line: she murdered the royal heirs and seized the throne for six years, until the priest Jehoiada crowned the hidden boy Joash and had her put to death (2 Kings 11).

judah.name: Joash
judah.evaluation_quote: Jehoash did that which was right… all his days wherein Jehoiada the priest instructed him
judah.summary: Hidden from Athaliah as a baby and crowned at seven, he restored the temple — but did right only while Jehoiada the priest instructed him (2 Kings 12:2). After the priest died he fell away, and his own servants killed him.

judah.name: Amaziah
judah.evaluation_quote: right in the sight of the LORD, yet not like David his father
judah.summary: Did right, yet not like David (2 Kings 14:3). He defeated Edom, then rashly challenged the North and was routed at Beth-shemesh, Jerusalem's wall breached; later he too was assassinated.

judah.name: Azariah (Uzziah)
judah.evaluation_quote: he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD
judah.summary: A long, prosperous 52-year reign of building and expansion — clouded when he was struck with leprosy and lived apart while his son Jotham governed (2 Kings 15:5).

judah.name: Jotham
judah.evaluation_quote: he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD
judah.summary: A capable, righteous king who built the upper gate of the temple (2 Kings 15:35). Assyria's shadow lengthened over Judah as his reign closed.

judah.name: Ahaz
judah.evaluation_quote: did not that which was right in the sight of the LORD his God, like David
judah.summary: Refused Isaiah's sign of Immanuel and, pressed by Israel and Aram, bought Assyria's protection — making Judah a vassal and setting a foreign-style altar in the temple (2 Kings 16; Isaiah 7).

judah.name: Hezekiah
judah.evaluation_quote: right in the sight of the LORD, according to all that David his father did
judah.summary: The great reform king — he tore down the high places and even the bronze serpent (2 Kings 18:4). When Assyria's Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem (701 BC) the city was spared, and his tunnel still carries the Gihon's water into the city.

judah.name: Manasseh
judah.evaluation_quote: he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, after the abominations of the heathen
judah.summary: Judah's longest-reigning king (55 years) and, in Kings, its most wicked — he rebuilt the high places and filled Jerusalem with innocent blood (2 Kings 21). The record lays Judah's coming ruin at his feet (2 Kings 23:26).

judah.name: Amon
judah.evaluation_quote: that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, as his father Manasseh did
judah.summary: A short reign in his father Manasseh's mold, cut off by a palace conspiracy after two years (2 Kings 21:23).

judah.name: Josiah
judah.evaluation_quote: right… walked in all the way of David his father, and turned not aside
judah.summary: The reform king at the heart of this story: the scroll found in the temple launched a sweeping purge, and he defiled Jeroboam's altar at Bethel (2 Kings 22–23). He fell at Megiddo confronting Egypt's Pharaoh Necho.

judah.name: Jehoahaz
judah.evaluation_quote: evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his fathers had done
judah.summary: Reigned three months before Pharaoh Necho deposed him and carried him to Egypt, where he died (2 Kings 23:31–34).

judah.name: Jehoiakim
judah.evaluation_quote: evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his fathers had done
judah.summary: Set on the throne by Egypt, then a grudging Babylonian vassal — he burned Jeremiah's scroll of prophecy (Jeremiah 36). His revolt brought Nebuchadnezzar's armies down on Judah.

judah.name: Jehoiachin
judah.evaluation_quote: evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his father had done
judah.summary: Reigned three months, then surrendered Jerusalem to Babylon (597 BC) and went into exile with the leading families. His release from a Babylonian prison (~561 BC) is the closing scene of the book of Kings (2 Kings 25:27–30).

judah.name: Zedekiah
judah.evaluation_quote: evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that Jehoiakim had done
judah.summary: Judah's last king — Babylon's appointee who rebelled once too often. Jerusalem fell in 586 BC; he saw his sons killed, then was blinded and dragged to Babylon (2 Kings 25:7).

israel.name: Jeroboam I
israel.qualifier: instituted the calves at Dan & Bethel
israel.summary: The North's founding king. To keep his people from Jerusalem he set golden calves at Dan and Bethel with a homemade priesthood (1 Kings 12) — 'the sin of Jeroboam' by which every northern king after him is judged.

israel.name: Nadab
israel.evaluation_quote: evil… walked in the way of his father, and in his sin
israel.summary: Jeroboam's son; within two years Baasha assassinated him and wiped out Jeroboam's whole line (1 Kings 15:27–29) — the North's first dynasty already gone.

israel.name: Baasha
israel.evaluation_quote: evil… walked in the way of Jeroboam
israel.summary: Seized the throne by killing Nadab and reigned 24 years, warring with Judah — but he walked in the way of Jeroboam, and his house was doomed to the same violent end.

israel.name: Elah
israel.qualifier: no explicit formula; slain by Zimri
israel.summary: Baasha's son, murdered while drinking by his chariot officer Zimri (1 Kings 16:9–10) — the second northern dynasty extinguished.

israel.name: Zimri
israel.evaluation_quote: his sins… doing evil… in walking in the way of Jeroboam
israel.summary: Reigned just seven days. When the army proclaimed Omri instead, Zimri burned the palace down around himself (1 Kings 16:18).

israel.name: Omri
israel.evaluation_quote: Omri wrought evil in the eyes of the LORD, and did worse than all before him
israel.summary: A powerful king who founded Samaria as the northern capital — so dominant that Assyria still called Israel 'the House of Omri' generations later. Judging worship, the text says he did more evil than any king before him.

israel.name: Ahab
israel.evaluation_quote: Ahab… did evil in the sight of the LORD above all that were before him
israel.summary: With his Sidonian queen Jezebel he made Baal a state cult — the age of Elijah and the contest on Mount Carmel. A formidable warrior-king, he died in battle at Ramoth-gilead (1 Kings 22).

israel.name: Ahaziah
israel.evaluation_quote: evil… walked in the way of his father, his mother, and Jeroboam
israel.summary: Ahab's son; injured in a fall, he sought the god of Ekron rather than the LORD and was rebuked by Elijah (2 Kings 1). He died within two years, without an heir.

israel.name: Joram
israel.evaluation_quote: wrought evil… but not like his father… put away the image of Baal
israel.summary: Ahab's son — he put away the Baal pillar but kept Jeroboam's calves. His reign is the age of Elisha; Jehu killed him in the coup that ended Ahab's house (2 Kings 9:24).

israel.name: Jehu
israel.evaluation_quote: took no heed to walk in the law… departed not from the sins of Jeroboam
israel.summary: Anointed at Elisha's word to purge Ahab's house, he swept away Jezebel, Ahab's line, and the Baal cult (2 Kings 9–10) and founded the North's longest dynasty. Assyria's Black Obelisk shows him paying tribute — yet he kept Jeroboam's calves.

israel.name: Jehoahaz
israel.evaluation_quote: evil… followed the sins of Jeroboam… he departed not therefrom
israel.summary: Jehu's son, ground down by Aram's Hazael until his army was almost nothing — until the LORD sent a deliverer (2 Kings 13:4–5).

israel.name: Jehoash
israel.evaluation_quote: evil… departed not from all the sins of Jeroboam
israel.summary: Recovered lost towns from Aram, as the dying Elisha foretold with the arrows (2 Kings 13:14–19). He also crushed Judah's Amaziah and breached Jerusalem's wall.

israel.name: Jeroboam II
israel.evaluation_quote: evil… departed not from all the sins of Jeroboam
israel.summary: The North's longest and most powerful reign (41 years) — he restored Israel's borders to their widest extent (2 Kings 14:25). His golden age of prosperity is the very wealth Amos and Hosea condemned.

israel.name: Zechariah
israel.evaluation_quote: evil… he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam
israel.summary: Jehu's last heir; after six months Shallum struck him down in public (2 Kings 15:10), ending Jehu's dynasty exactly as the LORD had said — to the fourth generation.

israel.name: Shallum
israel.summary: Reigned one month before Menahem killed him and took the throne (2 Kings 15:14).

israel.name: Menahem
israel.evaluation_quote: evil… departed not… from the sins of Jeroboam
israel.summary: Seized power brutally, then bought off Assyria's Pul with a thousand talents of silver, taxed from the North's wealthy men (2 Kings 15:19–20) — Assyria now at the door.

israel.name: Pekahiah
israel.evaluation_quote: evil… departed not from the sins of Jeroboam
israel.summary: Menahem's son, killed after two years by his own captain, Pekah (2 Kings 15:25).

israel.name: Pekah
israel.evaluation_quote: evil… departed not from the sins of Jeroboam
israel.summary: Took the throne by coup and joined Aram to pressure Judah — the crisis that drove Ahaz to Assyria. In answer, Tiglath-Pileser stripped away Galilee and Gilead and deported their people (2 Kings 15:29).

israel.name: Hoshea
israel.qualifier: last N king; 722 fall to Assyria
israel.evaluation_quote: evil… but not as the kings of Israel that were before him
israel.summary: The North's last king. His gamble on Egypt against Assyria brought Shalmaneser's siege; Samaria fell in 722 BC and Israel was carried into exile (2 Kings 17) — the Northern Kingdom was no more.
